[MUQATIL:16:77-78/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | People are born knowing nothing, and God subsequently teaches them.
[MUQATIL:16:77-78/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The hearts are what is meant by the faculties called afʾida.
[MUQATIL:16:77-78/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | They should thank the Lord for these blessings of fine creation by affirming His oneness.

[TAB-FULL:v14p315/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | After birth, God teaches people what they did not know and gives them reason to understand and distinguish good from evil; He enables them to see and hear after they had known nothing.
[TAB-FULL:v14p315/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Hearing receives sounds and lets people understand one another's conversation; sight sees people, allowing recognition and distinction between them.
[TAB-FULL:v14p315/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The afʾidah are hearts by which people know and retain things, reflect on them, and understand them.
[TAB-FULL:v14p315/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God bestowed these faculties so people would thank Him alone, not idols or partners that had no share in His blessings; the phrase is cited also at 2:52. | mentions 2:52
[TAB-FULL:v14p315/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The birth clause is a complete statement, followed by a new clause about the faculties; physical faculties were given before birth, but knowledge and reason after birth.

[RAZI-FULL:v20p71#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | أمهات derives from أمات by adding hāʾ, as in أراق/أهراق; its addition in the singular is rare, as the cited verse line shows.

[RAZI-FULL:v20p72/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Repeated seeing and hearing imprint the sensed things’ forms in imagination; the other senses similarly supply particulars for the mind.

[RAZI-FULL:v20p73/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The conjunction does not require temporal order; alternatively, hearing and sight can mean listening and seeing, removing the chronological objection.
